title: Jordan — Nabataean Stone, Bedouin Hosts and the Dana Descent
subtitle: Thirteen days from Roman Jerash through Dana's juniper cliffs to Petra's back trails and a Bedouin camp at Beidha
summary: A mostly self-drive route from Amman through Dana and Feynan to Petra, built around walking, Bedouin hosts and archaeology, and kept out of France Diplomatie's orange zones. Security status is conditional because of Iranian strikes on Jordan in 2026, recent attacks and conflicting official advice.
introduction: The trip starts in Roman Jerash and Byzantine Madaba, then crosses the inland plateau to Umm ar-Rasas and climbs into the Dana reserve, where a guided walk descends from a stone village to a candle-lit ecolodge at Wadi Feynan. From Wadi Musa, one day goes to Petra's Siq and Monastery, then two nights in a Bedouin-run camp at Beidha give Little Petra and the quiet back trail. The route stays on King's Highway and the Desert Highway north of Al-Hasa, away from Aqaba, Wadi Rum, Ma'an, the Dead Sea shore and the north-east. Ramadan ends before the March window.

exceptional.vsOman: Oman is a self-drive camping trip on gravel and dunes; here the camping is Bedouin-hosted at Beidha, the fixed stages are archaeological, and a walking descent from Dana to Feynan replaces driving as the centre of the trip.
exceptional.vsPackageTourism: Standard Jordan circuits visit the Treasury in a morning and leave. This one adds the Dana-Feynan descent, Little Petra and the Petra back trail, a Feynan Bedouin-run lodge night and two nights at a Bedouin camp beside Petra, with flexible days.
exceptional.vsPortfolio: Few portfolio destinations combine a Nabataean capital, a walkable biosphere reserve and UNESCO Byzantine sites within 4-5 hours of one international airport.

duration.note: Day 1 outbound and Day 13 return flights; 12 nights.

recommendedTravelWindow.rationale: Starts after Eid al-Fitr (about 9-11 March) so Ramadan opening-hours and crowding effects are over; milder days, drier than February, Petra comfortable. Mujib Siq Trail still closed (reopens spring).

februarySuitability.summary: Ramadan (about 8 Feb-9 Mar) shortens daytime food and shop access; Petra can be wet or snowy; nights in Dana and Beidha can approach freezing; Wadi Mujib and many canyons closed; flash-flood risk highest.

marchSuitability.summary: Mild days and cool nights. Rain and flash floods still possible; Eid holiday at the start brings domestic crowds, so the window begins on 12 March.

climate.regionNote: Rough Guides and aggregator figures for Amman and Petra; official Jordan Meteorological Department normals were not reachable. Petra and Dana are cooler than Amman because of altitude.

february.rainfall: Amman about 48-60 mm; Petra wettest in Jan-Feb
february.notes: Frost possible in Dana and Beidha at night; snow possible on the plateau.

march.rainfall: Amman about 30 mm; lower in Petra

climate.snowAndMountainAccess: Snow can close roads around Petra and the King's Highway (FCDO) in winter; March risk is low but not zero.
climate.seaConditions: Not relevant: no sea or Dead Sea leg after the redesign.
climate.airQuality: Generally good in the desert; dust events possible.
climate.wildlifeSeasonality: Spring migration of raptors and storks through the Rift Valley; Nubian ibex possible in Dana (not guaranteed).

holidaysAndFestivals.name: Ramadan

holidaysAndFestivals.name: Eid al-Fitr
holidaysAndFestivals.impact: Public holiday; domestic travel peaks at Petra and Madaba; book ahead or start after 12 March.

climate.ramadan2027: Ramadan ends about 9 March, so a 12-24 March trip avoids it. February would fall inside it: restaurants and food stalls mostly closed by day, reduced hours, and no evening Petra programming guaranteed.
climate.lunarNewYear2027: Not relevant: no Lunar New Year effect on Jordan.
climate.tourismDemand: Foreign arrivals at Petra were slightly down in 2026 (Jan-Sep 362,215 visitors, -2.8% year on year, per a trade site); local operators may offer discounts but availability is not constrained.
climate.flightPriceSeasonality: March fares are average; fares and schedules to the region are volatile because of the conflict.

geography.summary: The Rift Valley edge from Dana at 1,200 m down to the Wadi Feynan desert, then Petra's sandstone canyons and the inland Moab steppe.
geography.distinctive: One day's walk drops through four bioclimatic zones from Dana's juniper plateau to the desert wadi of Feynan; the next day's cliff-carved Petra sits in the same escarpment.

travelStyle.summary: Self-drive on King's Highway and Desert Highway, guided hiking days and Bedouin-hosted camping.

transport.summary: Rental car covers Amman, Jerash, Madaba, Umm ar-Rasas, Dana, Shobak and Wadi Musa; Feynan uses the lodge 4x4; the Petra back trail is on foot.

modes.description: Amman pick-up days 3-12; Desert Highway to Al-Hasa, King's Highway (Route 35) from Tafilah to Wadi Musa.
Airport and Amman downtown; Wadi Musa to Beidha.

transport.carRental: International brands operate at Queen Alia airport; some require a credit card deposit, minimum age about 21 and one year of licence; additional drivers may be added. One-way rental fees were not verified.

drivingRequirements.summary: Self-drive is feasible on main roads; night driving and winter conditions are the main hazards.
drivingRequirements.internationalDrivingPermit: Sources conflict: Sixt requires an IDP only for non-Roman-script licences, others say it is legally required; carry one if the licence country requires it.
drivingRequirements.licenceNotes: Two of the four hold car licences and share driving as additional drivers on the rental contract.
drivingRequirements.motorcycleNotes: No motorcycles or scooters. Use rental car, taxis, lodge 4x4 and guided walks.
drivingRequirements.recommendedApproach: Drive only in daylight, keep the car in Dana during the Feynan night, and avoid Ma'an, Karak and the Dead Sea road.

accommodation.summary: Guesthouses in Amman, Madaba, Dana and Wadi Musa; Feynan Ecolodge; Bedouin camp at Beidha.

camping.summary: Two nights in a Bedouin-run camp at Beidha beside Little Petra; Dana's Rummana campground is closed until March (date not verified); no wild camping planned.

physicalDifficulty.label: demanding
physicalDifficulty.summary: Long hiking days (Dana-Feynan 15 km, Petra 12-18 km, Jebel Haroun) and cold nights, but no technical skills.

itinerary.summary: Thirteen days: Amman and Jerash, Madaba and Umm ar-Rasas, inland road to Dana, Feynan night, Petra with Little Petra and a two-night Bedouin camp at Beidha, return to Amman with a buffer day. Redesigned on 27 Nov 2026 to keep out of France's orange zones (no Wadi Rum, Dead Sea or Highway 15 south of Al-Hasa).

security.summary: Conditional, close to the excluded line. France Diplomatie (Sécurité page updated 30 Oct 2026; zone text 22 Jul 2026) lists as orange ('déconseillé sauf raison impérative') the city of Ma'an, the strip beside the Syria/Iraq red zone, the border zone with the Palestinian territories, the north-east and Aqaba and its surroundings. The route was redesigned on 27 Nov 2026 to stay out of all of these: Wadi Rum (Aqaba governorate, orange-adjacent), the Dead Sea shore, Mount Nebo and Highway 15 through Ma'an were removed. The remaining reasons for 'conditional' are conflicting official advice (US Level 3 and Smartraveller reconsider vs FCDO 3 km and Dutch yellow), Iranian strikes on Jordan in 2026 with a fragile truce, two lethal attacks in October-November 2026, and one unresolved item (Feynan is about 25 km from the Israeli border; width of the French border zone not stated).
security.assessedRoute: Queen Alia Airport - Amman - Jerash - Madaba - Umm ar-Rasas - Desert Highway to Al-Hasa - Tafilah - Dana - Wadi Feynan - King's Highway/Shobak - Wadi Musa/Petra/Little Petra/Beidha - King's Highway north via Tafilah and Al-Hasa - Amman. Excludes Wadi Rum, Aqaba, the Dead Sea shore and Mount Nebo, Ma'an city, Karak city, Azraq, Mafraq, Zarqa/Rusayfah, Umm Qais and the border strips.

advisories.level: Orange (déconseillé sauf raison impérative): Ma'an city, the strip next to the Syria/Iraq red zone, the border zone with the Palestinian territories, the north-east and Aqaba with its surroundings (Iranian missile and drone fire since 17 July); red: Syria and Iraq borders. Zone text 22 Jul 2026, page 30 Oct 2026
advisories.regionsAffected: Ma'an city; Jordan Valley/Dead Sea border zone with the West Bank (width not stated); north-east incl. Azraq/Mafraq; Aqaba and surroundings
advisories.routeImpact: Route redesigned to avoid every orange zone: Wadi Rum (Aqaba governorate) and the Dead Sea float/Mount Nebo were removed, and the return runs north via Tafilah and Al-Hasa instead of the Desert Highway through Ma'an. Residual question: Feynan lies about 25 km from the Israeli border (border-zone width not stated).

advisories.routeImpact: Conflicts with FCDO and Dutch yellow advice.

conflictRisk.note: Jordan is not a party to the war but its airspace and bases (Azraq, Aqaba, Mafraq area) have been repeatedly targeted by Iranian missiles and drones from Feb to at least 9 Sept 2026; Jordan reported 261 of 281 intercepted over five weeks; debris fell in Azraq; US-Iran truce 'on life support' as of early Nov.

terrorismRisk.note: 23 Oct 2026 church shooting in Karak governorate (nine killed); 5 Nov 2026 stabbing in central Amman; border-crossing attacks in 2024-2025; FCDO says tourist sites are likely targets.

kidnappingRisk.note: No kidnapping advisory found for the route; not independently searched beyond the advisories cited.

regionalRestrictions: Avoid Azraq, Mafraq, Aqaba city, Zarqa/Rusayfah, border strips and any military/strategic sites (debris).
Airspace may close at short notice; shelter in windowless closed room when sirens sound.
Stays over 14 days require police registration (Jordan Pass holders exempt per France Diplomatie).
Do not add Wadi Rum, the Dead Sea shore or Aqaba back to the route unless France Diplomatie narrows its orange zones in writing.
Daylight transit only; no stop in Ma'an city or Karak city; avoid Highway 15 south of Al-Hasa.
Confirm with RSCN and the French embassy that Wadi Feynan is outside the orange 'zone frontalière avec les territoires palestiniens' (about 25 km from the border).
ordinaryRisks: Flash floods in wadis (Nov-Mar): no canyoning, check forecasts, do not drive wadi roads after heavy rain.
Winter snow/ice on the King's Highway and Petra roads.
Road safety: night driving, livestock, speed bumps; avoid driving after dark.
Pickpocketing and aggressive touts at tourist sites; use Careem/Uber rather than yellow taxis.
Petra and Beidha: cold nights, dehydration, scrambling injuries.
security.medicalAccess: Amman has private hospitals with good standards; Petra, Dana and Beidha are 1-4 hours from them. Evacuation insurance required.
security.insuranceConsiderations: Confirm in writing that the policy covers war/missile-related disruption and terrorism, and is not voided by official 'reconsider travel' advice (US, Australia). Trekking cover for guided hikes. Many Dutch insurers adjust cover for orange zones.
security.reassessmentRequired: Re-check all five advisories before booking and two weeks before departure. Reclassify to excluded if: Iranian strikes on Jordan resume or the US-Iran truce collapses; FCDO or Dutch advice extends 'all but essential' to Petra, Dana or Amman; France extends its orange zones to Petra, Dana, Feynan, Madaba or Umm ar-Rasas; any further attack on tourists or tourist sites; Jordanian airspace closes for extended periods; or insurers refuse cover.

practicalRequirements.visa: Conditional on nationality; many travellers get a visa on arrival (about 40 JOD) which the Jordan Pass waives if bought before arrival and minimum nights are met (2-3 nights, sources conflict).
practicalRequirements.entry: Check with the Jordanian embassy; keep return flight proof.
permits: RSCN reservations for Dana/Feynan guided activities
practicalRequirements.insurance: Travel insurance with evacuation, trekking and conflict wording check.
practicalRequirements.connectivity: Mobile coverage in towns; patchy in Dana-Feynan and Beidha; local SIM recommended.
practicalRequirements.payments: Cards in Amman; cash needed in Feynan, Beidha and small restaurants; ATMs mainly in cities.
practicalRequirements.medical: Standard travel vaccinations; France Diplomatie notes measles cases rising.
practicalRequirements.fuel: Fuel stations along the Desert Highway and King's Highway; fill up before Dana.
equipment: Warm layers and sleeping-bag liner for Dana and Beidha nights
Day packs and 3 L water capacity

advantages: All stops within 5 hours of one airport.
Strong archaeology plus real walking days.
Local ecolodge and Bedouin hosts for cultural contact.
March avoids Ramadan and most heat.
Route avoids every French and Dutch orange zone.
disadvantages: Security status is conditional with an active regional conflict and recent terror incidents.
Wadi Rum and the Dead Sea are excluded after the redesign; Wadi Mujib Siq Trail closed in winter.
uncertainties: Whether Iranian strikes on Jordan or the US-Iran truce change before March 2027.
Smartraveller level not re-read; France's orange 'zone frontalière' width and 'environs' of Aqaba are undefined (matters only if Wadi Rum or the Dead Sea were re-added).
Jordan Pass minimum stay and prices; Petra by Night schedule; Dana-Feynan guide rules; availability and standards of Bedouin camps at Beidha.
Whether Feynan (about 25 km from the Israeli border in Wadi Araba) lies inside the French border zone.
